Part 1 in Pictures

Part 1’s argument in eight pictures, in the order the chapter makes it. Hover, tap, or click any part of a chart for the explanation; each chart’s sources sit behind its footer link.

Consumer prices rose about 88 percent from the end of 1999 to the end of 2024.

By 2025 the federal interest bill was back at about 3.2 percent of GDP, level with its 1991 peak, on more than twice the debt.

For about two decades, from roughly 2000 to 2021, stocks and bonds tended to move in opposite directions, so bonds cushioned equity losses.

In 2022 a 60/40 mix of US stocks and bonds fell about 16 percent: stocks lost about 18 percent with dividends, and bonds, the part meant to cushion them, lost about 13 percent.

Same returns, same withdrawals, different order: at a 4 percent withdrawal, losses first ends with less than half what gains first ends with; at 6 percent it runs out in year 12.

ACF sizes exposure so the left tail is survivable and leaves the right tail free to run, within the concentration limits.

After a tripwire fires and its signal is verified, the response is one of four: watch, hedge, trim, or exit and redeploy.

Buying a fixed amount of Bitcoin every month from January 2018 to December 2024, through falls of more than 70 percent in 2018 and again in 2021 and 2022, still ended at about seven times the money put in.
